title: GCLI-12b: code-map tier 3, symbols resolved through the index, with dedupe and displacement
description: Child of GCLI-12, split confirmed by the leader on 2026-11-17 after the worker's size read (the whole is well over the ~400-line ceiling). Builds to opum-doc DEC-216 (a4) and opum-cli's CodeMapProducer seam (opum-ai/opum-cli dev, src/context/code-map.ts, and ADR 0008), read by ref only. Q1 (port versus merge) was ruled A in DEC-216 (a6) and 12a landed as GCLI-41. Slice b of three, after 12a: tier 3 per DEC-216 (a4). Symbols named in the task text, resolved through the index to their declaring files (score 0), plus the depth-1 impact of those symbols (score 1). Tier order is named paths, changed files, glyph, git-grep identifiers; a file in several tiers keeps its highest tier; ties break by score then path. The task-text-to-symbol-name rule (Q2) was ruled in DEC-216 (a6); both rulings are recorded verbatim in the implementation notes.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A task naming a symbol imported through an alias, which grep misses, finds its file in tier 3.
A file in more than one tier appears once at its highest tier; a mutation dropping the tier dedupe makes exactly the multi-tier file appear twice.
A fixture where tier 3 displaces a grep-only file at the 20-file cap records the displaced file under omissions.
With glyph disabled the output is the tiers 1, 2 and 4 output unchanged; bun run check passes.

implementationNotes: Carried from GCLI-41's close-out, to fold into this PR where it touches the same files: the hostile-config parity test needs a positive control (an assertion that git config core.quotepath reads false under the hostile GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL), the cli.test.ts over-cap test title should say UTF-16 code units, and the README sentence about the seam never reading the working tree's history should say it never reads uncommitted changes (tier 2 reads HEAD implicitly).

DEC-216 (a4)(c), verbatim:
"(c) RANKING: A, with one change: glyph's tier sits ABOVE the git-grep tier, not below it.
- Tier order: (1) named paths, (2) changed files, (3) glyph: symbols named in the task text, resolved through the index to their declaring files (score 0), plus the depth-1 impact of those symbols (score 1), (4) git-grep identifiers.
- A file found in more than one tier keeps its highest tier.
- Ties break by score, then path, exactly as in opum-cli ADR 0008.
- Why above grep: a symbol resolved through the type checker is a stronger signal than a text match. Putting it last would let grep noise fill the 20-file cap before glyph's answer appears.
- The fallback stays a true control: with glyph absent or failing, the output is byte-identical to the deterministic producer's.
PROOF:
- glyph off gives byte-identical output to the deterministic producer;
- a fixture where the task names a symbol imported through an alias, which grep misses and glyph finds in tier 3;
- a fixture where tier 3 displaces a grep-only file at the cap, recorded under omissions;
- mutation control: dropping the tier-3 dedup makes exactly the multi-tier file appear twice."

DEC-216 (a6) GCLI-12 Q2, verbatim: "A. Reuse the deterministic producer's identifier extraction. Match index symbols by EXACT name, and when a name matches several symbols, include them all (each counted). Qualified and fuzzy matching are out of scope for v1."

Review round 1 (Opus, 323d0f3), M1 evidence: in the exactly-one-multi-tier fixture (decl.ts declared plus grep-matched; user.ts tier-3 only with one hit; note.ts grep only) the dedup mutant (tier-3 candidates keyed apart by path) adds exactly one extra pointer, a second src/decl.ts, and no other path repeats; test 'exactly one file found by two tiers appears once' is the one that reddens. Parity scope: the byte parity with opum-cli's producer (GCLI-41, #80) covers the deterministic tiers (named paths, changed files, identifiers), run with symbols:false or an absent or throwing index loader; the CLI's default output adds tier 3 and is not claimed byte-identical to the producer.

DEC-216 (a9), verbatim:
"The \"score 0 / score 1\" in (a4)(c) was DISTANCE, not ADR 0008's score. Within tier 3 the order is:
1. distance ascending (the declaring file, then depth-1 callers);
2. ADR 0008's score, higher first;
3. path.
A declaring file always outranks its callers, which is the point of the tier.

One condition, for the contract. The emitted pointer's `score` field (if the seam carries one) keeps ADR 0008's meaning everywhere: higher means stronger. Distance must NOT be written into `score`, because a consumer compares scores across tiers and producers. If glyph emits distance at all, it goes in its own field or in the pointer's reason text. Please have glyph-cli confirm which it did. If distance went into `score`, that's a small fix before GCLI-37 closes."
glyph-cli confirmation: the seam's pointer has no score field (keys are path, lineRanges, reason, pinned by test). Distance is emitted only in the reason text (declares symbol / depth 1); internally it is a separate Candidate.distance, and Candidate.score keeps ADR 0008 meaning (churn, or distinct identifiers matched, higher first).

Close-out. Landed as opum-ai/glyph-cli#84, squash 678c5fdc12cfa70a6bd6ccee3ca80c70da0e7e17 on dev (reviewed head a12aa1f, Opus APPROVE; round 1 REQUEST CHANGES at 323d0f3 resolved at 49e3c3c; DEC-216 (a9) folded at a12aa1f). CARRIED TO GCLI-38, non-blocking: (1) test/parity.test.ts hostile-config test: the plain-config tier-3 run reuses the index the hostile run cached (shared GLYPH_CACHE_DIR), so the index build is never compared across configs; use a separate cache dir per run. (2) test/cli.test.ts cache-hit test: nothing confirms the second run was a HIT; assert a cache .json exists after the miss. (3) src/codemap.ts ranking comment 'by source (paths, then branch, then identifiers)' omits the symbol tier.
finalSummary: Tier 3 landed in opum-ai/glyph-cli#84 at 678c5fd (reviewed head a12aa1f). See the close-out note for the items carried to GCLI-38.
